(This is a long post, but I provide a summary, Σ, at the bottom.) I have retained my present lap-top computer, a _HP Pavilion dv6-7010us Entertainment PC_, that runs Windows 7 with 64 bits, since I purchased it in 2012. Occasionally its track-pad becomes unresponsive, apparently spontaneously; I have sometimes observed it occur after the lap-top is moved off of its desk, yet sometimes it occurs even when stable. I keep Mouse Keys permanently enabled; it can occasionally rectify this problem, but equally often does not, and sometimes is even likewise unresponsive. Re-starting the computer ordinarily does not help, nor does re-installing the track-pad's drivers. If the computer is re-started in this condition, the cursor holds fast at the precise centre of the screen after Windows starts. The period between incidents like this may be measured in minutes or days; it occurs at least once weekly.

The only certain solution that I have found is to remove the battery and disconnect the charging chord and re-start the computer. This typically functions, though occasionally it requires several attempts, for the cursor may nonetheless hold fast in the centre. I have observed that the cursor may hold fast if not moved soon after Windows starts, though this may well be incidental. This is obviously not ideal.

-------

*I proceed hence to note the historical development of this problem, and sundry issues relating to my laptop and this issue. I apologise for the length.*

This problem first appeared approximately a year after I purchased the computer [*id est* shortly after the warranty expired], but then only occasionally and tolerably after right-clicking. Only in the last year (rather approximately— my memory is alas poor) has this problem occurred more frequently and spontaneously.

Since last January my computer has been more susceptible to over-heating and hence shutting down without warning; streaming high-definition video or playing _Sid Meier's Civilisation V_ for perhaps 30 minutes will crash the computer, though this has never happened before and does not occur elsewhere. I am led to suspect this is because I exchanged my lap-top's broken stand for a new one I received as a Christmas gift; my former stand was raised and allowed air to reach underneath, but my new one does not. It feels howbeit important to note this here.

Approximately two months ago I enabled Mouse Keys, that my computer may remain usable even if the mouse holds fast; as noted above, it has mixed success and scarcely allows me to use the track-pad again.

Some three weeks ago another strange development occurred after one session that I removed the battery. After replacing the battery in its socket I found it apparently no longer works; the laptop would detect a fully charged battery (and the BIOS diagnostics would indicate that it was fully usable and not defective), yet the laptop would immediately shut off if disconnected from the mains. It also disconnected from my wireless Internet network; after hours of undirected clicking and using a new mobile phone, that I incidentally received upon the following day, as my tether, I resolved this problem, though the problem of the battery remains.

Occasionally after being unplugged many times, it is apparently necessary, though I find no discernible effect in any case, after start-up to 'check discs for consistency'; typically the New Technology File Service (NTFS). This process typically resolves some errors but may sometimes shut off the computer partly through the process. After either one or several runs it completes the process, though 'normal' function is unchanged regardless of whether it proceeds.

I have since removed the battery entirely and I keep my lap-top on my desk and connected to the mains, rendering it practically a desk-top. There have been no complications with the wireless Internet, though occasionally the mouse holds fast as noted above.

-------

Σ / *Summary.* — My lap-top's cursor may without warning become unresponsive; this sometimes occurs once a week, but may transpire several times within an hour. Unplugging my computer, sometimes several times, is the only definitive solution that I have found. Re-installing the track-pad drivers has not resolved this, but this is apparently a problem of software, for disconnecting and reconnecting the mains indeed resolves the problem temporarily. After one such routine where I unplugged the computer, the battery is non-functional; it appears charged when connected, but the computer now shuts off if separated from the mains.

I sincerely thank the Voat community for any help that you can provide with this chronic and disruptive issue.

Heat is the enemy of electronics. Heat damage is CUMULATIVE. The damage caused does not "heal." It just gets worse with each overheating incident. If your laptop is getting too hot, you need to do whatever you can to keep it cool. Dirt and dust are the prime culprits here. Vacuum/blow out all the dirt and dust you can from the vents and fans. And replace that stand with a cooling pad that has fans. The more airflow the better.

By shutting down the laptop forcibly, you are damaging the hard drive. Each time, you are creating a "data pot hole" on the drive. The disk checks are patching the pot holes the best they can, but eventually, your "road" is going to be full of patches. It's a vicious cycle: The more pot holes you have, the more likely you are to hit them. The more you hit them, the bigger/more numerous the pot holes become.

Your battery is likely bad. Those BIOS diagnostics are not 100% reliable. If the battery is more than a few years old, then it's time to replace it...especially given the symptoms you describe.
